grh_f09dff0f4387773b3b5f.title: Vienna Three and Four
paragraphs: English businessman Fred Carson arrives in Vienna to negotiate a large doll purchase and is seized by intelligence men who insist he is the spy known as Vienna Three. After escaping, he takes refuge with airline stewardess Agnes Brown, while freelance operative Harold Cox closes in on a microdot containing the names of more than a thousand American agents in West Germany. Fred eventually reveals that the mistaken identity was no mistake: he really is Vienna Three, the genuine microdot is in his possession, and he and Agnes have arranged its sale while using earlier operatives as decoys. Cox boasts that he killed Vienna One and arranged the fatal crash that killed Vienna Two. Fred then reveals that Vienna Two was his daughter. The final confrontation leaves Fred wounded, and he sends Agnes to escape through Vienna's sewers while he remains behind.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on July 6, 1979. It is listed as episode 110 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Antoinette Bower, Barney Phillips, Fletcher Markle, Hans Conried, and Ivor Barry. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Alan Caillou as writer, and [[person|howard-duff|Howard Duff]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_f0cfa15aa3068dd7a325.title: Words at War 43-10-26 (20) Who Dare to Live
paragraphs: Merchant captain Jack returns from wartime service physically recovered but shaken by the loss of a ship and crew, and fears that no company will trust him with another command. Given the freighter Sarah, he struggles through delays, crew trouble and a difficult Atlantic voyage while trying to prove he still belongs at sea. After reaching Halifax, he admits how much the ordeal has cost him. Told he needs rest rather than another command, Jack finally accepts that serving the merchant fleet in another capacity is still honorable service and agrees to go back to work.

grh_f04e72dd40bb27341574.title: Its in the Bag
paragraphs: Flea-circus operator Fred Floogle learns that his murdered Uncle Trumbull supposedly left him $300,000 hidden in one of a set of chairs that were sold at auction. Fred and his family chase the chairs from owner to owner while criminals and the uncle's lawyer Jefferson T. Pike pursue the same prize. The final chair exposes Pike as the uncle's killer and preserves the evidence against him, but Fred's hoped-for cash fortune turns out to be something else entirely: Trumbull's $300,000 is tied up in a murder story he wrote called Its in the Bag.
